locations.name: Dubrovnik, Croatia
clues: A queen did a very long, very naked walk of shame down a staircase here. Shame. Shame. Shame.
Its old town played King’s Landing in Game of Thrones.
A walled city on the coast of Croatia, across the Adriatic from Italy.
locations.fact: The city now limits cruise ships because so many fans turned up.

locations.name: Hobbiton, New Zealand
clues: You can get a pint at the Green Dragon here, but mind your head on the way in.
Bilbo’s round green front door is still set into the hillside.
A sheep farm on the North Island of New Zealand.
locations.fact: The set was built twice. The first one was polystyrene and got pulled down.

locations.name: Barry Island, Wales
clues: Oh! What’s occurring?
Gavin is from Essex. Stacey is from here, and Nessa works the slots in the arcade.
A seaside resort in South Wales, just along the coast from Cardiff.
locations.fact: Nessa’s booth in the arcade is still there, and you can sit in it.

locations.name: Mallorca, Spain
clues: A place for grafting, cracking on, and getting pied in front of the nation.
Every summer a villa here fills up with singles in swimwear who’d like a chat.
The Love Island island: the biggest of Spain’s Balearics.
locations.fact: It’s also where you’ll find Magaluf, so it has seen things.

locations.name: Glenfinnan Viaduct, Scotland
clues: A flying Ford Anglia nearly gets flattened by a steam train here.
The Hogwarts Express crosses this curving viaduct on the way to school.
It’s in the Scottish Highlands, a little west of Fort William.
locations.fact: A real steam train, the Jacobite, still crosses it every summer.

locations.name: Skellig Michael, Ireland
clues: Luke Skywalker spent his retirement sulking on this rock.
It was so covered in puffins that the film crew turned them into porgs.
A jagged island off the south-west tip of Ireland, in County Kerry.
locations.fact: Monks lived on the summit for 600 years, in stone huts shaped like beehives.

locations.name: Birmingham, England
clues: By order of the Peaky Blinders.
Tommy Shelby’s gang ran the back streets of Small Heath in this city.
England’s second city, home of the Bullring, Cadbury and a great many canals.
locations.fact: It really does have more miles of canal than Venice.

locations.name: Albuquerque, New Mexico
clues: A chemistry teacher here found a far better-paid use for his skills.
Home of Walter White, Jesse Pinkman and Los Pollos Hermanos.
The biggest city in New Mexico, in the desert of the south-west USA.
locations.fact: Fans keep throwing pizzas onto the roof of the real house. The owners have asked them to stop.

locations.name: Chernobyl, Ukraine
clues: “3.6 roentgen. Not great, not terrible.”
Reactor number four exploded here in April 1986.
It’s in the north of Ukraine, close to the border with Belarus.
locations.fact: The town next door, Pripyat, still has a fairground that never opened.

locations.name: Skopelos, Greece
clues: Meryl Streep ran a crumbling hotel here, and her daughter had three possible dads.
Mamma Mia! Here we go again: the film was shot on this island.
A Greek island in the Aegean Sea, north of Athens.
locations.fact: The little chapel on the rock has 199 steps, which is a lot in a wedding dress.

locations.name: Ardross Castle, Scotland
clues: A round table, a lot of cloaks, and a woman with a very heavy fringe.
It’s the castle from The Traitors.
In the Scottish Highlands, a short drive north of Inverness.
locations.fact: Nobody actually sleeps there. The players are driven to a hotel every night.

locations.name: Seoul, South Korea
clues: 456 players, one giant piggy bank, and a very tense game of Red Light, Green Light.
Squid Game is set in this capital city, which also gave the world K-pop.
The capital of South Korea.
locations.fact: About half of all South Koreans live in or around it.

locations.name: Derry, Northern Ireland
clues: Erin, Orla, Clare, Michelle, and the wee English fella.
Derry Girls. There’s a mural of them on the side of a pub.
A walled city in the north-west of Northern Ireland, right by the border.
locations.fact: Its city walls have never been breached, which is why it’s called the Maiden City.

locations.name: Matmata, Tunisia
clues: Luke Skywalker grew up in a hole in the ground here. It’s now a hotel.
The desert planet Tatooine is named after a real town just down the road.
In the south of Tunisia, on the northern edge of the Sahara.
locations.fact: You can still eat breakfast in the Skywalkers’ dining room.

locations.name: Kauai, Hawaii
clues: “Welcome to Jurassic Park.” The helicopter lands beside a waterfall on this island.
It’s nicknamed the Garden Isle, and it belongs to the USA’s surfiest state.
One of the Hawaiian islands, in the middle of the Pacific.
locations.fact: A real hurricane hit during filming. Some of the storm in the film is genuine.

locations.name: Scranton, Pennsylvania
clues: Home of the World’s Best Boss, according to his own mug.
The Dunder Mifflin Paper Company has its branch here.
A small city in Pennsylvania, in the north-east of the USA.
locations.fact: That’s what she said.

locations.name: The I’m a Celebrity jungle, Australia
clues: Every November, famous people come here to eat things that should not be eaten.
Ant and Dec watch from a treehouse while somebody shouts “Get me out of here!”
It’s on the east coast of Australia, in the hills behind the Gold Coast.
locations.fact: The camp is a fifteen-minute drive from a perfectly nice town with a pub.

locations.name: Medellín, Colombia
clues: “Plata o plomo?” Silver or lead?
In Narcos, Pablo Escobar runs his cartel from this city.
Colombia’s second city, up in the Andes in the north-west of South America.
locations.fact: Escobar’s escaped pet hippos have bred. There are now well over a hundred.

locations.name: New York City, USA
clues: Six friends drank a lot of coffee here, in a flat none of them could afford.
The one with Central Perk, the Empire State Building and the yellow taxis.
The Big Apple, on the east coast of the USA.
locations.fact: Friends was filmed in Los Angeles. The fountain is on a studio lot in California.

locations.name: Ibiza, Spain
clues: A café here got famous for sunsets and sold millions of chill-out CDs to your parents.
Pacha, Amnesia and Ushuaïa are all on this island. The Vengaboys were going.
A Spanish party island in the Mediterranean, off the coast of Valencia.
locations.fact: Its seagrass meadows are a World Heritage Site, and one of the oldest living things on Earth.

locations.name: Benidorm, Spain
clues: Full English breakfasts, mobility scooters, and a tribute act every night of the week.
The ITV sitcom set at the all-inclusive Solana resort is named after it.
A wall of skyscrapers on Spain’s Costa Blanca.
locations.fact: It has more high-rise buildings per person than anywhere else on Earth.

locations.name: Malia, Crete
clues: Will, Simon, Jay and Neil came here on their first lads’ holiday. It went badly.
The Inbetweeners Movie made its strip of bars famous.
A party resort on the north coast of Crete, the biggest Greek island.
locations.fact: It also has a 3,500-year-old palace, which gets rather fewer visitors.

locations.name: Amsterdam, Netherlands
clues: The first suggestion in every stag-do group chat.
Canals, more bikes than people, and coffee shops that aren’t really about the coffee.
The capital of the Netherlands.
locations.fact: Around 12,000 bikes are fished out of its canals every year.

locations.name: Ayia Napa, Cyprus
clues: A fishing village that became the summer home of UK garage in about 2000.
Nissi Beach by day, the square full of bars by night.
A resort at the south-east corner of Cyprus, in the far east of the Mediterranean.
locations.fact: It has a museum of underwater sculptures you can only visit with a snorkel.

locations.name: Koh Phangan, Thailand
clues: Buckets, glow paint, a flaming skipping rope, and regret.
Tens of thousands of backpackers pile onto its beach every month for the Full Moon Party.
An island in the Gulf of Thailand.
locations.fact: The first Full Moon Party, in the 1980s, was about thirty people and a guitar.

locations.name: Bali, Indonesia
clues: Half your Instagram feed has been on a swing over a rice terrace here.
Canggu for the smoothie bowls, Ubud for the yoga, Uluwatu for the surf.
An Indonesian island, just east of Java.
locations.fact: Once a year the whole island shuts for a day of silence. Even the airport closes.

locations.name: Glastonbury Festival, England
clues: For most of the year it’s a dairy farm.
Then 200,000 people turn up, and none of your mates managed to get tickets.
Worthy Farm in Somerset, home of the Pyramid Stage.
locations.fact: A ticket to the first one in 1970 cost £1 and came with free milk.

locations.name: Las Vegas, Nevada
clues: What happens here, stays here.
The Hangover: a tiger in the bathroom, a missing groom, and a fake Eiffel Tower outside.
A city of casinos in the desert of Nevada, in the western USA.
locations.fact: The famous Strip isn’t technically in Las Vegas. It’s in a town called Paradise.

locations.name: Prague, Czech Republic
clues: A city where a pint has long been cheaper than a bottle of water.
A stag-do favourite with a medieval astronomical clock and a very old bridge.
The capital of the Czech Republic.
locations.fact: Czechs drink more beer per person than any other country, and it’s not close.

locations.name: Budapest, Hungary
clues: George Ezra would give up his house here for you. He had never been.
Ruin bars, thermal baths, and a river that splits the city in two.
The capital of Hungary, on the Danube.
locations.fact: It used to be two cities: Buda on one bank, Pest on the other.

locations.name: Dubai, UAE
clues: Where influencers go when they announce they’re ‘relocating for business’.
It has the world’s tallest building, and an island shaped like a palm tree.
A city in the United Arab Emirates, on the Persian Gulf.
locations.fact: The Burj Khalifa is so tall you can watch the sunset twice: once at the bottom, once at the top.

locations.name: Marbella, Spain
clues: “No carbs before Marbs.”
The cast of TOWIE come here every summer to argue beside a pool.
A glitzy resort on Spain’s Costa del Sol, not far from Málaga.
locations.fact: Its marina, Puerto Banús, has more supercars than parking spaces.

locations.name: Munich, Germany
clues: Six million people come here every autumn and drink seven million litres of beer.
Lederhosen, pretzels and steins the size of your head: it’s Oktoberfest.
The capital of Bavaria, in the south of Germany.
locations.fact: Oktoberfest mostly happens in September.

locations.name: Reykjavík, Iceland
clues: Everyone you know has a photo in a milky-blue lagoon near here, wearing a face mask.
In 2010 a volcano nobody could pronounce grounded every flight in Europe. It’s in this country.
The capital of Iceland.
locations.fact: It’s the most northerly capital city in the world.

locations.name: Sydney, Australia
clues: Everyone on a working holiday visa ends up here, sharing a flat with six other Brits.
Bondi Beach, a harbour bridge, and an opera house that looks like a pile of sails.
Australia’s biggest city, on the south-east coast.
locations.fact: It isn’t the capital. That’s Canberra, which was built to stop this city and Melbourne arguing.

locations.name: Santorini, Greece
clues: White houses, blue domes, and a queue of couples waiting to photograph the sunset.
It’s shaped like a croissant, because it’s the rim of a volcano that blew itself up.
A Greek island in the Aegean, between Athens and Crete.
locations.fact: The eruption, 3,600 years ago, may be where the legend of Atlantis comes from.

locations.name: Rovaniemi, Lapland
clues: A man here gets more post than anyone else on Earth, almost all of it in December.
It’s the official home town of Father Christmas, right on the Arctic Circle.
The capital of Lapland, in the north of Finland.
locations.fact: Santa’s post office has had letters from 198 countries.

locations.name: Blackpool, England
clues: Every Strictly couple is desperate to make it to this town’s ballroom.
A Pleasure Beach, three piers, six miles of illuminations and a lot of rock.
A seaside resort in Lancashire with a tower that isn’t quite the Eiffel.
locations.fact: The tower is 158 metres tall. The one it copied is about twice that.

locations.name: Loch Ness, Scotland
clues: Home of Britain’s most camera-shy resident.
It holds more water than every lake in England and Wales put together, and possibly a monster.
A long, deep loch in the Scottish Highlands, south-west of Inverness.
locations.fact: The most famous photo of Nessie was a toy submarine with a plastic head.

locations.name: Stonehenge, England
clues: Nobody is sure who built it or why, but you get a decent look from the traffic jam on the A303.
A ring of enormous standing stones, about 5,000 years old.
On Salisbury Plain in Wiltshire, in the south of England.
locations.fact: Some of the stones were dragged 150 miles from Wales.

locations.name: Liverpool, England
clues: It hosted Eurovision in 2023, on behalf of Ukraine.
Four lads with guitars, two cathedrals, and two birds on top of a building.
A port city on the River Mersey, in the north-west of England.
locations.fact: Legend says that if the Liver Birds ever fly away, the city will cease to exist.

locations.name: Newcastle upon Tyne, England
clues: The first ever Greggs opened in a suburb of this city.
Home of Ant and Dec, Geordie Shore, and a night out with no coat on.
A city on the River Tyne, in the north-east of England.
locations.fact: The Tyne Bridge was built by the same firm as the Sydney Harbour Bridge.

locations.name: Giant’s Causeway, Northern Ireland
clues: Legend says a giant called Finn McCool built it so he could walk to Scotland for a fight.
About 40,000 stone columns, nearly all of them neat hexagons.
It’s on the north coast of Northern Ireland.
locations.fact: It’s actually cooled lava, about 60 million years old.

locations.name: Edinburgh, Scotland
clues: Every August it fills up with comedians handing out flyers.
It has a castle on an extinct volcano, and a very loud Hogmanay.
The capital of Scotland.
locations.fact: A cannon is fired from the castle at one o’clock, so the whole city can set its watch.

locations.name: Newquay, Cornwall
clues: Where half the country went the week after their GCSEs.
Britain’s surf capital: Fistral Beach and the Boardmasters festival.
A seaside town on the north coast of Cornwall.
locations.fact: Its airport is also a licensed spaceport.

locations.name: Yr Wyddfa (Snowdon), Wales
clues: There’s a café at the top, and a train if you can’t be bothered.
The highest mountain in Wales.
It’s in Eryri National Park, in the north-west corner of Wales.
locations.fact: Edmund Hillary trained here before climbing Everest.

locations.name: Isle of Man
clues: Its flag has three legs on it, and its cats have no tails.
Every summer motorbikes race round its ordinary roads at 200 miles an hour.
An island in the middle of the Irish Sea, between England and Ireland.
locations.fact: It isn’t part of the UK, and its parliament is over a thousand years old.

locations.name: Alton Towers, England
clues: You queued two hours here for ninety seconds of screaming.
Nemesis, Oblivion and The Smiler: Britain’s biggest theme park.
In Staffordshire, in the middle of England.
locations.fact: The Smiler turns you upside down fourteen times, which is a world record.

locations.name: Manchester, England
clues: Its symbol is a worker bee, and it rains rather less than people say.
Oasis, the Haçienda, and two football teams whose fans would like a word with each other.
A big city in the north-west of England, half an hour inland from Liverpool.
locations.fact: The first stored-program computer ran here in 1948. They called it the Baby.

locations.name: John o’ Groats, Scotland
clues: People walk, cycle and occasionally skateboard 874 miles to get here.
It’s the other end of the journey from Land’s End.
A village at the far north-east tip of mainland Scotland.
locations.fact: It’s not actually the most northerly point. That’s Dunnet Head, eleven miles away.

locations.name: Dover, England
clues: There’ll be bluebirds over them, according to the song.
Famous for white cliffs and for queues of lorries waiting for a ferry.
A port in Kent, at the closest point of England to France.
locations.fact: On a clear day you can see the French coast, 21 miles away.

locations.name: Brighton, England
clues: The seagulls here will take the chips right out of your hand.
A pier, a pebble beach, a palace that looks like the Taj Mahal, and a very big Pride.
A seaside city on the south coast, an hour from London.
locations.fact: In 2002 Fatboy Slim played a free gig on the beach. A quarter of a million people came.

locations.name: Dublin, Ireland
clues: A pint in its most famous bar district will cost you about a tenner.
Home of Guinness, Temple Bar and a statue everybody calls the Tart with the Cart.
The capital of Ireland.
locations.fact: The Guinness brewery’s lease runs for 9,000 years, at £45 a year.

locations.name: Belfast, Northern Ireland
clues: “She was fine when she left here,” they say of the city’s most famous ship.
The Titanic was built in its shipyard. Line of Duty was filmed on its streets.
The capital of Northern Ireland.
locations.fact: The two giant yellow shipyard cranes are called Samson and Goliath.

locations.name: St Andrews, Scotland
clues: A prince met his future wife at the university here.
It’s known as the home of golf.
A small town on the east coast of Scotland, north of Edinburgh.
locations.fact: People have played golf on its Old Course for about 600 years.

locations.name: Glasgow, Scotland
clues: There’s a statue here that has worn a traffic cone on its head for forty years.
Celtic, Rangers, Irn-Bru and the deep-fried Mars bar’s spiritual home.
Scotland’s biggest city, on the River Clyde.
locations.fact: The council once planned to raise the statue to stop the cone. The city said no.

locations.name: Machu Picchu, Peru
clues: The Spanish conquered the whole empire and never found this place.
A lost city of the Incas on a mountain ridge, with llamas wandering into your photos.
High in the Andes in Peru.
locations.fact: It was built without wheels, iron tools or mortar, and it has survived 500 years of earthquakes.

locations.name: The Pyramids of Giza, Egypt
clues: The only one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World that’s still standing.
Three enormous pointy tombs, guarded by a Sphinx with no nose.
On the edge of Cairo, in Egypt.
locations.fact: Cleopatra lived closer in time to the iPhone than to the building of the Great Pyramid.

locations.name: Uluru, Australia
clues: Most of it is underground, like an iceberg made of sandstone.
A giant red rock, sacred to the Anangu people. Climbing it was banned in 2019.
Almost exactly in the middle of Australia.
locations.fact: It changes colour through the day, and glows bright red at sunset.

locations.name: Mount Everest
clues: On a busy day there’s a queue for the top.
The highest mountain on Earth.
In the Himalayas, on the border between Nepal and Tibet.
locations.fact: It grows by about four millimetres a year.

locations.name: The Taj Mahal, India
clues: Princess Diana was photographed sitting alone on a bench in front of it.
A white marble tomb built by a heartbroken emperor for his favourite wife.
In the city of Agra, in northern India.
locations.fact: It took 20,000 workers and a thousand elephants about twenty years.

locations.name: Niagara Falls
clues: Jim and Pam from The Office got married on a boat here.
In 1901 a 63-year-old teacher went over the edge in a barrel, and lived.
A giant waterfall on the border between Canada and the USA.
locations.fact: Engineers can turn the flow down at night, and they do.

locations.name: Christ the Redeemer, Brazil
clues: He gets struck by lightning several times a year.
A giant statue with open arms on a mountaintop, looking down on Copacabana beach.
In Rio de Janeiro, on the coast of Brazil.
locations.fact: In 2014 a lightning strike took off the tip of his thumb.

locations.name: Petra, Jordan
clues: Indiana Jones found the Holy Grail inside its most famous building.
A rose-red city carved straight into the cliffs about 2,000 years ago.
In the desert in the south of Jordan.
locations.fact: Behind the grand front of the Treasury there’s just one small, empty room.

locations.name: The Great Wall of China
clues: No, you can’t see it from space.
Over 13,000 miles of it were built to keep invaders out.
The most-visited stretch is just north of Beijing.
locations.fact: The mortar in some sections was made with sticky rice.

locations.name: Mount Fuji, Japan
clues: It’s the mountain on the emoji keyboard. 🗻
A perfectly cone-shaped volcano with snow on top that hasn’t erupted since 1707.
South-west of Tokyo, in Japan.
locations.fact: There’s a post office at the summit.

locations.name: The Grand Canyon, Arizona
clues: It’s a mile deep, and it took a river about six million years.
The most famous hole in the ground in America.
In Arizona, in the south-west USA.
locations.fact: You could stack four Shards in it and still not reach the rim.

locations.name: Area 51, Nevada
clues: In 2019 two million people signed up to storm it. “They can’t stop all of us.”
A secret air base where the US government definitely isn’t keeping any aliens.
In the desert of Nevada, in the western USA.
locations.fact: About 150 people actually turned up. Nobody got in.

locations.name: Bermuda
clues: Ships and planes are said to vanish in the triangle named after it.
It also gave its name to a pair of knee-length shorts.
A tiny British island territory in the Atlantic, about 650 miles off the east coast of the USA.
locations.fact: Its beaches really are pink, thanks to the crushed shells of tiny red sea creatures.

locations.name: The wreck of the Titanic
clues: “I’m the king of the world!”
There was room for Jack on that door. The ship went down here in April 1912.
The North Atlantic, about 400 miles off Newfoundland, Canada. Yes, it’s in the sea.
locations.fact: She lies two and a half miles down, and wasn’t found until 1985.

locations.name: Pompeii, Italy
clues: Bastille asked how they were going to be an optimist about this.
A Roman town buried by a volcano in AD 79, graffiti and all.
Beside Mount Vesuvius, near Naples in southern Italy.
locations.fact: The graffiti is mostly insults, adverts and people boasting about their love lives.

locations.name: The Leaning Tower of Pisa, Italy
clues: Everybody here is taking exactly the same photo.
A bell tower that started to tilt before the builders had even finished it.
In Tuscany, in the north of Italy.
locations.fact: It took 199 years to build, which gave it plenty of time to lean.

locations.name: The Eiffel Tower, France
clues: It was only meant to stay up for twenty years, and the locals hated it.
A 330-metre iron tower that sparkles on the hour, every hour, after dark.
Paris.
locations.fact: It’s about fifteen centimetres taller in summer, because the iron expands.

locations.name: Bran Castle, Transylvania
clues: Bring garlic.
It’s sold to tourists as Dracula’s castle.
In Transylvania, in the middle of Romania.
locations.fact: Bram Stoker never went to Romania. He wrote much of Dracula in Whitby.

locations.name: Alcatraz, California
clues: Al Capone did time here, and played banjo in the prison band.
An island prison nobody is known to have escaped from alive.
In San Francisco Bay, on the west coast of the USA.
locations.fact: The inmates had hot showers, so they’d never get used to cold water and try the swim.

locations.name: The Hollywood Sign, California
clues: It started out as an advert for a housing estate, and had four more letters.
Nine white letters on a hillside, each one four storeys tall.
Los Angeles, on the west coast of the USA.
locations.fact: In 1976 a prankster changed it to read HOLLYWEED.

locations.name: Victoria Falls
clues: Its local name means ‘the smoke that thunders’.
You can swim in a pool right on the edge, if you’re feeling brave.
A giant waterfall in southern Africa, on the border between Zambia and Zimbabwe.
locations.fact: The spray can be seen from thirty miles away.

locations.name: Cape Town, South Africa
clues: The mountain behind it is so flat that the cloud on top is called the tablecloth.
Winter Love Island moved in nearby. The penguins on the beach were there first.
A city near the southern tip of Africa.
locations.fact: Table Mountain is about six times older than the Himalayas.

locations.name: Angkor Wat, Cambodia
clues: Angelina Jolie raided a tomb here, and the tree roots have nearly eaten it.
The biggest religious building in the world. It’s on its country’s flag.
In the jungle of Cambodia, in south-east Asia.
locations.fact: It was built as a Hindu temple and gradually became a Buddhist one.

locations.name: Shibuya Crossing, Japan
clues: Up to 3,000 people cross the road here every time the lights change.
Neon, giant video screens, and a statue of a very loyal dog called Hachikō.
Tokyo.
locations.fact: Hachikō waited at the station for his owner every day for nearly ten years.

locations.name: Easter Island, Chile
clues: A Dutch explorer landed here on a Sunday in spring and named it after the day.
It’s watched over by nearly a thousand giant stone heads, like the 🗿 emoji.
A tiny speck in the Pacific, over 2,000 miles west of Chile.
locations.fact: The statues are called moai, and most of them have bodies buried below the ground.

locations.name: Zanzibar, Tanzania
clues: A spice island whose old quarter is called Stone Town.
The singer of ‘Bohemian Rhapsody’ was born here.
It lies in the Indian Ocean, just off the east coast of Africa.
locations.fact: It was once the world’s biggest producer of cloves.

locations.name: Mauritius
clues: Sailors stopping here for supplies ate a large, trusting, flightless bird.
It was the only home the dodo ever had.
A honeymoon island in the Indian Ocean, to the east of Madagascar.
locations.fact: The dodo was extinct within about a century of people arriving.

locations.name: Port Royal, Jamaica
clues: Once called the wickedest city on Earth.
Jack Sparrow sails into it on a sinking boat at the start of the first film.
It guards the harbour of Kingston, on the Caribbean island famous for reggae.
locations.fact: Two thirds of the real Port Royal slid into the sea in an earthquake in 1692.

locations.name: Nassau, Bahamas
clues: For about a decade this town was the capital of a self-declared Republic of Pirates.
Blackbeard, Calico Jack and Anne Bonny all drank here.
Today it’s the capital of the Bahamas, just off the coast of Florida.
locations.fact: The pirate republic ended in 1718 when Governor Woodes Rogers arrived offering royal pardons.

locations.name: Tortuga, Haiti
clues: Its name means ‘turtle’, after the shape of the island.
It’s where Jack Sparrow goes to find a crew, and a slap.
It sits just off the north coast of Haiti, in the Caribbean.
locations.fact: The real buccaneers here called themselves the Brethren of the Coast.

locations.name: Île Sainte-Marie, Madagascar
clues: This island has what’s said to be the world’s only pirate cemetery.
Pirates used it to ambush ships sailing home from India.
It lies off the east coast of Madagascar, the big island off Africa with the lemurs.
locations.fact: As many as a thousand pirates are thought to have lived here around 1700.

locations.name: Ocracoke Island, North Carolina
clues: A thin strip of sand in a chain of barrier islands.
Blackbeard fought his last battle here in November 1718.
It’s on the east coast of the USA, about halfway between New York and Florida.
locations.fact: Legend says Blackbeard’s headless body swam around the ship three times.

locations.name: Cartagena, Colombia
clues: Spanish treasure fleets loaded up with gold and emeralds here.
Francis Drake captured the city in 1586 and held it to ransom.
A walled city on the Caribbean coast of Colombia, at the top of South America.
locations.fact: After the raids, Spain built the largest fortress in its American colonies here.

locations.name: Cape Horn, Chile
clues: Sailors feared this headland more than any other.
Tradition says rounding it earns you a gold earring.
It’s the very southern tip of South America.
locations.fact: Before the Panama Canal opened in 1914, this was the main sea route between the Atlantic and the Pacific.

locations.name: Galápagos Islands, Ecuador
clues: Buccaneers hid here and stocked their ships with live giant tortoises.
A young Charles Darwin visited in 1835 and took a keen interest in the finches.
These islands sit on the equator, about 600 miles west of South America.
locations.fact: ‘Galápago’ is an old Spanish word for tortoise.

locations.name: Robinson Crusoe Island, Chile
clues: A Scottish privateer was marooned here alone for over four years.
His story inspired a very famous novel about a castaway.
It’s in the Pacific, about 400 miles off the long thin coast of Chile.
locations.fact: The real castaway was Alexander Selkirk, rescued in 1709.

locations.name: Pitcairn Island
clues: One of the most remote inhabited islands on Earth.
Mutineers from HMS Bounty hid here in 1790 and burned their ship.
It’s in the South Pacific, roughly halfway between New Zealand and South America.
locations.fact: Around fifty people live here today, many descended from the mutineers.

locations.name: Oak Island, Nova Scotia
clues: People have been digging for treasure here since 1795 and found almost nothing.
It’s famous for a mysterious booby-trapped shaft called the Money Pit.
A small island on the Atlantic coast of Canada.
locations.fact: Theories about what’s buried here range from pirate gold to Shakespeare’s manuscripts.

locations.name: Cocos Island, Costa Rica
clues: Hundreds of expeditions have searched this jungle island for the lost Treasure of Lima.
Today it’s better known for hammerhead sharks than for gold.
It’s in the Pacific, about 340 miles off Central America.
locations.fact: Nobody has ever found the treasure. Or at least, nobody has admitted to it.

locations.name: Clew Bay, Ireland
clues: Home waters of a 16th-century pirate queen who met Elizabeth I face to face.
The bay is said to have an island for every day of the year.
It’s on the west coast of Ireland, in County Mayo.
locations.fact: Grace O’Malley commanded hundreds of men and a fleet of galleys from her castles here.

locations.name: Algiers, Algeria
clues: For three centuries this was the great stronghold of the Barbary corsairs.
The red-bearded Barbarossa brothers ruled from here.
A North African capital on the Mediterranean, directly south of Mallorca.
locations.fact: Barbary corsairs raided as far north as Cornwall, Ireland and even Iceland.

locations.name: Saint-Malo, France
clues: A walled port that grew rich on legal piracy.
Its corsairs raided English ships with the French king’s blessing.
It’s on the north coast of Brittany, a ferry ride from Portsmouth.
locations.fact: Its motto was roughly: ‘Not French, not Breton, but from Saint-Malo.’

locations.name: Panama City, Panama
clues: Captain Henry Morgan, the one on the rum bottle, sacked this city in 1671.
Spanish silver from Peru passed through here on its way to Europe.
Today a very famous canal starts right beside it.
locations.fact: Morgan was arrested for the raid, then knighted and made deputy governor of Jamaica.

locations.name: Charleston, South Carolina
clues: Blackbeard blockaded this entire port for nearly a week in 1718.
His ransom demand was not gold but a chest of medicine.
A historic harbour city on the east coast of the USA, a little north of Florida.
locations.fact: He got his medicine chest and sailed away without firing a shot.

locations.name: Hong Kong
clues: These waters were ruled by the most successful pirate in history, and she was a woman.
Zheng Yi Sao commanded hundreds of junks and tens of thousands of pirates.
A famous skyscraper-packed harbour city on the south coast of China.
locations.fact: She negotiated a pardon, kept her loot, and retired to run a gambling house.

locations.name: Wapping, London
clues: Execution Dock stood on the riverbank here for 400 years.
Captain Kidd was hanged at this spot in 1701.
It’s on the River Thames, in England’s capital.
locations.fact: Pirates’ bodies were left until three tides had washed over them.

locations.name: Bristol, England
clues: Blackbeard is believed to have been born in this port.
In ‘Treasure Island’, the Hispaniola sets sail from here.
A harbour city in the south-west of England, famous for Banksy, a suspension bridge and hot-air balloons.
locations.fact: Long John Silver ran the Spy-glass tavern on Bristol’s docks.

locations.name: Penzance, Cornwall
clues: A seaside town with a notorious smuggling past.
Gilbert and Sullivan wrote a comic opera about its pirates.
It’s almost at the very tip of Cornwall.
locations.fact: ‘The Pirates of Penzance’ opened in 1879 and has barely been off the stage since.

locations.name: Tahiti, French Polynesia
clues: HMS Bounty spent five months here collecting breadfruit plants.
The crew liked it so much that leaving helped spark the mutiny.
It’s the largest island of French Polynesia, in the middle of the South Pacific.
locations.fact: Captain Bligh survived a voyage of nearly 4,000 miles in an open boat after being cast adrift.

locations.name: Havana, Cuba
clues: Spanish treasure fleets gathered here every year before crossing the Atlantic.
Famous for cigars, rum and classic 1950s cars. Camila Cabello left her heart here.
It’s the capital of the largest island in the Caribbean.
locations.fact: A French corsair burned the city to the ground in 1555.
